_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Kinetic Scenes roadmap rendered at /kinetic-scenes/roadmap. Hand-maintained, and it lists OPEN work only: when a task is done, document it on its guide page under /kinetic-scenes/ and delete it from here (the 228 tasks of phases 1-29 were retired this way on 2026-11-20; the guide pages describe them). Update `extensionVersion` to the Studio version.

milestones.title: Capability shorts — one video per thing it can do
milestones.goal: A short vertical video (up to a minute) for each of the 40 things in Help › What Kinetic Scenes can do, showing the feature working and the prompt that made it. Each is made in Kinetic Scenes, posted to YouTube Shorts, Facebook and Instagram, and its YouTube id added to the list, so the start box’s Did you know? tip plays it for returning visitors. Made in batches of five, in the Unyson+ look and the Jon 4 voice, built to a preview link and rendered only when asked.

tasks.title: Shorts, batch 1: what people miss
tasks.detail: Cut the person out of your video; your screen on a 3D phone; a mascot that talks; a voice-over in your own voice; real 3D models with Blender.

tasks.title: Shorts, batch 2: let the AI make it
tasks.detail: Describe it, get a scene; turn a website into a video; cut a long video into a reel; make one like a video you like; a video for every row of a spreadsheet.

tasks.title: Shorts, batch 3: reel effects
tasks.detail: Talking-head effects (freeze frame, split push, LED sign); graphics that follow your face; ready-made pieces; captions word by word; moves that land on a word.

tasks.title: Shorts, batch 4: looks
tasks.detail: 55 styles; restyle anything; painted and hand-drawn; a paper cut-out explainer; things that fall and bounce.

tasks.title: Shorts, batch 5: products and finishing
tasks.detail: Product tours from a screen recording; charts, counters and code; animated heroes for your website; export in every shape; check the scene for you.

milestones.title: Phase 32 · Better 3D
milestones.goal: Better and wider 3D for scenes. Agents already build models and shots in Blender through the AI Dev Kit (blender_model, blender_render) and put them in 3D layers; this phase makes those models better, reaches shapes that scripted modelling cannot (a shoe, a plant, a character), and lets you work in a live Blender window when you want to. Each tool is optional and is switched on in the AI Dev Kit's Tools section, planned with the kit.

tasks.title: Screencasts of phone apps
tasks.detail: Record real Android apps for product tours and client reels: mirror and record an Android phone over USB with scrcpy (the Android Studio emulator when no phone is at hand), and bring the recording in as footage with the screencast tools. iPhone apps: the phone's own screen recording or mirroring it to the computer, since the iOS Simulator runs only on a Mac. The tools themselves are switched on in the AI Dev Kit's Tools section.

milestones.title: Still open from earlier phases
milestones.goal: The few tasks left from phases 1-29. Everything else from those phases is built and described on the guide pages.

tasks.title: Load media near the playhead
tasks.detail: Live scenes fetch each part's pictures and footage as the playhead nears it (the opening first, then ahead), showing the poster frame until then, instead of loading everything when the page opens. Needs a new player version and the Kinetic Scene element to use it. Already done (Studio 0.1.78): play waits, with a loading ring, for the footage, pictures and sounds the next few seconds need, and footage that stalls holds the scene.

tasks.title: Benchmark against hand-made videos
tasks.detail: Rebuild reference motion-graphics videos from their voice-overs with the new tools and compare them frame by frame, the way the Site Converter is measured against its sources, until the Studio's version holds up next to them. Round 1 rebuilt a 10-second side-by-side race explainer from the new pieces and fixed what it found (pills sized to their words, Change text resizing them smoothly); round 2 compares it frame by frame with the reference. Round 2 waits for the reference video.

tasks.title: Paste a link
tasks.detail: Paste a video link to make one like it, or to learn its rhythm only. The source is studied and then deleted, never reused, and captions are read first.

tasks.title: Watch a video
tasks.detail: A video_watch tool for agents, with a frame budget, a focus range and frames pinned to cues.

milestones.title: Later, deferred or only if people ask
milestones.goal: Cloud options that wait until people ask for projects across computers. Until then, projects stay in the browser and as folders on your computer.

tasks.title: Picture to 3D model (trial)
tasks.detail: Try LATO.2 (MIT code and weights), an open picture-to-mesh model, for shapes scripts cannot model: a photo or an AI picture becomes a mesh, Blender cleans it up (decimate, materials, GLB) and it lands in a 3D layer. It needs a CUDA graphics card with more memory than this machine's 6 GB, so the trial also tests its hosted demo and a rented GPU before deciding. Deferred (2026-11-26): the model wants more graphics memory than the 6 GB card here; revisit with a bigger card or when people ask.

tasks.title: Save to Google Drive
tasks.detail: Projects on any computer without our own server: people sign in with Google and their scenes are saved to their own Drive. Planned if people ask for cross-device projects. Needs a Google OAuth client ID from the site owner before it can be built. Deferred (2026-10-29): not planned until people ask for it; projects stay in the browser and as files.

tasks.title: Accounts and cloud projects (only if needed)
tasks.detail: If real accounts are ever needed (a project library, short links, embeds that update in place), they run on a free cloud tier, separate from the website hosting, with uploads on object storage and embeds still served from GitHub Pages. Deferred (2026-10-29): not planned until people ask for it; projects stay in the browser and as files.
